column1: Real-life competition formats for Touchline
A first draft of how each league, domestic cup, continental club competition and national-team tournament in Touchline works in real life.
Pegged to: the start of the 2026/27 season, or the 2026 season for calendar-year competitions.
Drafted from general football knowledge, not yet checked source by source. Treat Medium and Low rows as leads to verify.
How to use it
1. Work through the Low rows first, then Medium. Check each against the competition’s official site or its current season page.
2. Fill in the yellow columns: Source (a link) and Last verified (a date). These are the only columns meant for typing.
3. Grey columns on the Leagues sheet are read from Touchline (commit d4878f1, 8 Nov 2026); the last two columns compare them with real life automatically.
4. Repeat the check each summer: formats change most seasons.
Confidence
High: well established and stable.
Medium: believed correct; worth a quick check.
Low: uncertain or changes often; verify before relying on it.
Notes on the columns
Matches per club: the regular phase only (before any split or play-offs). For leagues with two tournaments (Apertura and Clausura), it is per tournament; the next column gives the season total.
Touchline format: one table, a split, Apertura/Clausura, play-offs or conferences, as the game currently plays it.

Regional sheet categories: A, top-flight clubs take part (Brazil); B, regional or island leagues that are the first stage of the national championship (New Zealand, Cape Verde); C, regional competitions for lower and amateur clubs only; D, none for top clubs today. Rows marked "not real" in the In Touchline column are regional cups the game generates that have no real-life equivalent for top clubs.

Cross-border clubs: clubs that play in another nation's league (Monaco in France, Welsh clubs in England, Canadian clubs in MLS and others). Touchline currently has none: every club in a league belongs to that league's nation.

Cross-nation leagues: leagues with clubs from more than one nation by design, active (MLS, the A-League, the OFC Pro League) and past (Royal League, Baltic League, African Football League, BeNe League, and the Soviet, Yugoslav and Czechoslovak leagues).

Cross-nation cups: active club cups and super cups, national cups that admit clubs from other nations, and historical cross-nation cups. Rows marked "fictional" in the In Touchline column are cups the game has with no real equivalent.

Fictional in Touchline: every competition in the game with no real equivalent (Fictional) or only a loose or irregular one (Partly fictional). The Domestic cups, Continental club and International sheets also have a "Touchline competition is" column.

Youth tournaments and cups: national-team youth tournaments (worldwide, continental, regional and invitational) and club youth cups (international and national). Youth leagues are not included. Touchline currently has none of these: its U21 and U18 club sides play youth leagues, and its Under-21 national teams play friendlies.

B teams: the Leagues sheet shows whether each senior league has B or reserve teams in real life, where they play instead if not, and how many Touchline has. Youth leagues are deliberately not included.

Youth requirements: the Leagues sheet shows real rules that make clubs register or field young or homegrown players: homegrown quotas, a young player on the pitch, a season minimum of minutes for young players, young players in the squad, or incentives only. Many of these rules change often, so most are marked Medium or Low.

Pro/rel play-offs: the Leagues sheet shows play-offs where a club from this league plays a club from the division above or below (e.g. the Bundesliga’s 16th v the 2. Bundesliga’s 3rd). Play-offs within one division, such as England’s Championship play-offs, are not counted here.

Second tiers: real second divisions beyond those on the Leagues sheet. Seven were added to Touchline in November 2026 (the Netherlands, Portugal, Brazil, Turkey, Poland, Norway and Sweden): they are now on the Leagues sheet and marked Yes here.

Third tiers: real third divisions. Touchline has only England’s, Spain’s and Germany’s (marked Yes); the rest are not in the game. Many third tiers are split into regional groups, so the club count covers all groups.

Fourth tiers: real fourth divisions. Touchline has only England’s (League Two, marked Yes). Most fourth tiers are regional groups of semi-professional or amateur clubs, so club counts are approximate and most rows are Low confidence.

Qualifying: how teams qualify for the main national-team tournaments, club competitions and domestic cups: the number and format of qualifying stages, who enters at which stage, how hosts are treated, and how Touchline does it.
Tie rules: single or two legs by stage, away goals, extra time, penalties, replays and finals for the main tournaments and cups.
International calendar: FIFA’s men’s windows for 2026–2030 (the merged four-match September/October window, then November, March and June), compared with Touchline’s two breaks.
Guest nations: tournaments that invite nations from outside their confederation or region (the Copa América and Gold Cup above all).

World Cup qualifying: every stage of each confederation’s qualifying, using the completed 2026 cycle as the template (teams per stage, format, dates, where the places go), the intercontinental play-off, and what is known about 2030.
